title: perf-canary: wire service account, secret storage, and least-privilege IAM
author: Nadia Rahman
body:
Summary: This PR adds the Terraform wiring needed to deploy perf-canary safely: (1) a dedicated service account with least-privilege IAM, (2) secret storage + access policies for canary auth, and (3) environment/region guardrails to prevent accidental fanout. This unblocks the perf-canary Helm chart rollout by providing a constrained identity that can call internal inference endpoints and emit metrics without broad access.

Context: perf-canary runs synthetic workloads against internal inference endpoints and publishes performance metrics/alerts. We need a dedicated identity for the canary deployment (no shared runtime/telemetry SA), scoped to: read-only inference invoke, write-only metrics, and read-only baseline artifact access. We also need to store the canary auth token / client secret in managed secret storage and allow only the canary workload identity to decrypt/access it.

What changed (high level): - Introduced perf_canary_service_account module (GCP) and associated IAM bindings. - Added Secret Manager secrets for perf-canary auth material and a KMS policy to allow decrypt only by the canary SA. - Added explicit IAM conditions and narrowed resource scopes (project/namespace/cluster) to avoid granting broad viewer/editor roles. - Added a small set of env/region toggles (enable_perf_canary, perf_canary_regions allowlist) and validation to avoid enabling canary in all regions by mistake.

IAM scope (intended): - Inference invoke: allow calling internal inference gateway (limited audience/scope; no general service-to-service). - Metrics: allow write to telemetry ingest (no read, no admin). - Baselines: allow read from baseline bucket/prefix only (no list on entire bucket, no write). - Secrets: allow access to perf-canary secret versions only (no create/delete; no wildcard).

Operational notes: - Secret rotation: this PR creates the secret resources and IAM; rotation procedures remain in the infra runbook. - Rollback: disabling perf-canary is done by setting enable_perf_canary=false in the environment tfvars; IAM resources remain but are inert.

Testing/verification: - terraform validate + fmt - terraform plan for staging-us-east and prod-us-east: no unexpected diffs outside perf-canary resources - Manual check: SA cannot list other secrets or buckets; can read only the one secret and baseline prefix.

Risk: Medium. IAM changes are production-impacting; however this PR only adds new bindings/resources (no removal of existing roles). Reviewers: please sanity-check IAM conditions and secret access boundaries.

Follow-ups: - Consider adding org-policy constraint to block secret access from non-approved service accounts (separate PR) - If we move baselines from GCS to config service, we should replace the bucket read binding accordingly.

Refs: Linear ENG-4879 (Deployment helm + terraform), ENG-4872 (MVP), ENG-4878 (alerting routing). Jira INT-2213 (service account permissions request).
commits: perf-canary: add service account + workload identity wiring
secret-manager: create perf-canary auth secret + iam binding
iam: restrict baseline bucket access to prefix + read-only
env: add perf_canary enable flag + region allowlist validation
docs: annotate outputs consumed by redwood-helm-charts
changed_files: modules/baselines/storage_iam.tf (add read-only prefix binding for canary)
checks: tfsec: pass (1 warning acknowledged: secret version replication default; tracked in ENG-4882)
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we ensure the canary can only write metrics and not query/modify telemetry configs? The role binding should be the ingest-only role, not project-level monitoring editor.

Nadia Rahman (author): Good catch. Updated modules/telemetry/iam_ingest.tf to bind roles/telemetry.ingestWriter (custom) instead of monitoring.editor. Also added an IAM condition restricting the audience to the ingest endpoint service.

Rafael Mendes (review): For INT-2213 we need to be explicit about what the canary can call. Is the inference invoke permission limited to the internal gateway only? Please avoid granting generic service invoker on all endpoints.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yep. Swapped to a per-service invoker binding on the inference-gateway-canary endpoint only (and added a TODO for private deployments where this will differ). No wildcard serverless invoker remains.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please add a kill switch / guardrail so we don't accidentally enable in every region during rollout. Also can we cap to us-east only for prod by default?

Nadia Rahman (author): Added enable_perf_canary boolean + perf_canary_regions allowlist with validation. Prod defaults are empty allowlist (disabled) until explicitly set in tfvars; staging set to ["us-east"].
Allison Grant (review): Secret access: please ensure only get access to this one secret and not list. Also prefer to deny secret destroy from the canary SA.

Nadia Rahman (author): Secret IAM binding is roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor on the single secret resource only; no list permission. Canary SA has no permissions to create/update/destroy secrets. Only platform-infra group retains admin.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we export the SA email + secret resource name as outputs for the Helm chart wiring? Want to avoid copy/paste in values files.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added outputs: perf_canary_service_account_email, perf_canary_secret_resource_id, perf_canary_baseline_bucket, perf_canary_baseline_prefix.
Logan Wright (approval): Looks good after role tightening. Thanks for adding the allowlist validation.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved; inference invoke is appropriately constrained now.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Guardrails are in place; proceed with staging rollout.
release_notes: Adds Terraform resources for perf-canary service account, secret storage, and least-privilege IAM bindings; introduces enable flag and region allowlist to prevent accidental global rollout.
